answer: Each identity posts one row on a public velvet table: claim, key, 70-credit bond. Each epoch auditors spiral outward from a random row; a copied row or one key on two rows burns both bonds. A row earns nothing until it survives the 10-epoch horizon. The k-th fake costs 40+6(k-1); 1,000 burn 3,037,000 and lock 70,000 for a 40,000 pool. Rented rows fail: one key on two rows in one epoch exposes them. Honest agents pay 40 once, keep the bond.
